tasks.short: Observe participants, note progress per goal, put notes in the care record, build a summary and discuss it with the care team.

steps.what: Recreation worker observes participants during activities
Recreation worker documents individuals' progress toward treatment goals after the activity: on paper today, as a level and a short note per goal on a tablet after the change
Recreation worker copies notes into the care record each week: all of them today; after the change only notes from sessions without a tablet
Recreation worker writes a progress summary for the care plan review: by hand today; after the change the system lists the levels per goal and the worker checks it and adds a short comment
Recreation worker discusses progress with the care team in the review meeting

tasks.design: After each activity the worker enters a level per treatment goal and a short note on a tablet in the care record system ({OTHER}), so only notes from sessions without a tablet are copied at the end of the week. The system lists the levels per goal for each participant, and the worker checks that list against the notes and adds a short comment for the care plan review; observing and discussing progress with the team stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were written on paper and copied into the care record weekly.
tasks.enabler_now: Care record systems hold goal-based entries on tablets and summarise them.
tasks.still_hard: Levels per goal are judgement; notes are health data with strict access.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a withdrawn resident join in for the first time and knowing what it means.

reach.learn: Whether goal entries make reviews shorter.

evidence.claim: Care record systems hold goal-based entries on tablets and build summaries.
Progress notes on treatment goals are health data; access must be limited to the care team.

assumptions: Boundary: from observing to the review meeting; setting goals is outside.
Input contract: treatment goals set by the care team in the care record; levels agreed by the activity team; fallback is paper notes.

Observing and discussing keep their full time. s2 keeps 90 because the worker still writes each level and note; only the participant and goal headings are filled. s3 keeps 10 for sessions without a tablet. s4 keeps 30 for reading the listed levels against the notes and writing the comment.
Entries are about participants, not used to judge staff.
unknowns: Participants with treatment goals per worker.
research_questions: Do care plan reviews use the activity entries?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: the care team sets the goals and levels in the record, and learning the entry screen is a one-off.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: tablets are at only half the sessions, so half the notes are still copied (13.5); high: tablets at most sessions (19.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Greet newcomers, introduce them, explain the rules, encourage them to join and register their details.

steps.what: Recreation worker greets new arrivals to activities
Recreation worker introduces newcomers to other participants and encourages participation
Recreation worker explains facility rules
Newcomer fills in contact and emergency details on the tablet form
Recreation worker registers newcomer details: writes them on a paper sign-up list today; checks the newcomer's own form after the change

tasks.design: Newcomers register themselves on a tablet form in the centre's participant system ({OTHER}) with contact and emergency details, and the worker only checks it. Greeting, introducing, explaining rules and encouraging stay fully in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Details were written on paper lists by the worker.
tasks.enabler_now: Self-registration forms on tablets are simple to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Some newcomers need help with the form.
tasks.human_edge: Making a shy newcomer feel they belong from the first minute.

evidence.claim: Self-registration forms on tablets record contact and emergency details.
Participant details are personal data; keep only what the centre needs.

assumptions: Boundary: from arrival to registration; activities are outside.
Input contract: form fields set by the centre manager; fallback is the paper list.
Greeting, introducing and explaining keep their full time. s4 keeps 30 for checking each form; helping those who cannot use the tablet is the upkeep below.
Participants' time, including filling in the form (s3n, share 1), is outside the worker's savings.

incremental.description: Recreation worker helps newcomers with the form.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many newcomers cannot use the tablet, so the worker fills about half the forms (5.1); high: most newcomers fill it in themselves (9.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Listen to the complaint, record it, discuss it with the manager, tell the participant the outcome and keep the complaints overview.

steps.what: Recreation worker listens to the participant's complaint
Recreation worker writes the complaint down: on paper today, in a short form with type and status after the change
Recreation worker confers with management to discuss and resolve the complaint
Recreation worker tells the participant the outcome
Recreation worker keeps a spreadsheet of complaints for the quarterly review

tasks.design: Complaints go into a short form in the centre's participant system ({OTHER}) with type and status, and the system keeps the overview for the quarterly review. Listening, conferring with the manager and telling the participant stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complaints were paper notes and a spreadsheet kept by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple complaint forms with status and overviews are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving complaints is people work; the form records it.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a participant is really upset about.

reach.learn: Whether complaint types show what to change.

evidence.claim: Complaint forms with type, status and overviews are simple records apps.
Complaints hold participants' personal data; keep them only as long as needed.

assumptions: Boundary: from the complaint to the outcome and overview; formal appeals are outside.
Input contract: complaint types set by the centre manager; fallback is paper.

Listening, conferring and telling keep their full time. s2 keeps 90 because the worker still writes the complaint; only type and status become picks. s5 goes because the system keeps the overview from the forms.
Manager time is outside the worker's savings.
research_questions: Are complaints closed faster with a status?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: the centre manager sets the complaint types, and learning the form is a one-off.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complaints told in passing still go on paper, so half the overview is kept by hand (2.5); high: all complaints go into the form (6.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect agenda items, meet with staff, write minutes, send them and follow up actions.

steps.what: Colleagues add their agenda items to the shared meeting page
Recreation worker collects agenda items: by e-mail today; after the change orders the items colleagues added on the page
Recreation worker meets with staff to discuss rules, regulations and work-related problems
Recreation worker writes the minutes: from handwritten notes after the meeting today, typed into the meeting page during the meeting and tidied afterwards after the change
Recreation worker checks the final minutes: agreements, owners and dates as decided in the meeting
Recreation worker publishes the checked minutes to all staff: by e-mail today, by one release of the meeting page with a notice after the change
Recreation worker follows up agreed actions with colleagues

tasks.design: A shared meeting page in {DOCS} lets colleagues add agenda items themselves, and minutes are typed into it during the meeting; the worker checks the final minutes and releases the page with a notice to staff. The meeting and follow-up stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agenda items came by e-mail and minutes were typed and mailed afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared document pages with notifications are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Colleagues must use the page; minutes still need writing.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a tired team to agree on how to handle a difficult rule.

reach.learn: Whether one page keeps agreements visible.

evidence.claim: Shared document pages let colleagues add items and notify readers on change.
Tools that log each staff member's actions can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from agenda to follow-up; decisions by management are outside.
Input contract: meeting page set up by the centre manager; fallback is e-mail.

The meeting, the check of the minutes and follow-up keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 for ordering and adding items. s3 keeps 70 because typing up handwritten notes goes, but writing and tidying the minutes stays. s4 keeps 25 for the release.
Colleagues' time, including adding items (s0, share 1), is outside the worker's savings.
research_questions: Do more colleagues bring agenda items?

incremental.description: Recreation worker types minutes during the meeting.

approvals.approved_version: The minutes exactly as checked by the worker in s3c, published once on the team's meeting page with a notice to all staff; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: colleagues keep e-mailing items and the worker cannot type during the meeting while chairing (6.8); high: items on the page and minutes typed live (14.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The recreation worker keeps activities, welcome and conversations; copying notes, lists and mailing minutes go.
role.ambitious_version: A recreation worker whose records are complete when the activity ends.
